current_f2_semantics.R3: adaptive selection among explicitly admitted R0/R1/R2 mechanisms
current_f2_semantics.selection_observation: R3 selects the first declared route-compatible and policy-admitted mechanism in a fixed policy preference order; this component does not inspect task payload text or infer task complexity and does not itself measure mechanism value, quality gain, latency or cost.

primary_sources.title: Recursive Language Models
primary_sources.authors: Alex L. Zhang; Tim Kraska; Omar Khattab
primary_sources.source_read: Paper abstract plus author-maintained repository README/source architecture surface.
primary_sources.finding: Recursive programmatic decomposition can improve long-context performance and can be cost-competitive, but the mechanism is an inference strategy around model calls rather than evidence that recursion is universally beneficial.

primary_sources.title: Recursive Language Models Meet Uncertainty: The Surprising Effectiveness of Self-Reflective Program Search for Long Context
primary_sources.finding: Program selection materially determines success; the authors report recursion is not the primary performance driver and can degrade relative to the base model for inputs within the model context window.

primary_sources.title: Recursive Agent Harnesses
primary_sources.finding: Harness recursion can outperform a fixed-backbone coding-agent baseline on a controlled long-context benchmark, supporting F2's distinction between model recursion and Native Child harness recursion while still requiring a matched F2 baseline.

primary_sources.title: ReCAP: Recursive Context-Aware Reasoning and Planning for Large Language Model Agents
primary_sources.finding: Hierarchical recursion benefits from structured parent-plan/context reinjection and bounded active context; this supports preserving parent-goal/handoff lineage across recursive return rather than treating recursion as context-free spawning.

positive_evidence: F2 already separates mechanism class from nested-child depth, matching the external distinction between model recursion and full harness recursion.
F2's explicit policy/admission/provenance boundaries are thinner and more authority-safe than importing the RLM execution framework wholesale.
RLM/RAH research establishes plausible benefit domains for R1/R2 rather than a requirement to prefer recursion globally.
counterevidence_and_gap: SRLM reports recursion can underperform the base model in some within-window conditions and attributes much of performance to program selection rather than recursion itself.
Current R3 uses declared availability plus static policy preference, not an observed expected-benefit-per-resource discriminator.
Repository component CI proves routing invariants, not that choosing R1 or R2 improves F2 task quality, token efficiency, latency or recovery over R0/direct execution.
External benchmark gains are not transferable as F2 runtime credit.
hypothesis: Before runtime promotion, WP603 should require a matched value/overhead evaluation contract: a recursive mechanism is selected for measured benefit only when it beats the cheapest compatible nonrecursive/direct baseline at declared quality and evidence constraints.
counterhypothesis: The higher-level upstream router/ControlSnapshot or later adaptive-compute layer will already supply all decision-relevant mechanism availability and value information, making a WP603-local value gate duplicate policy and create another arbitration authority.
next_discriminator: Map an evidence-only RecursionValueObservation/selection-input contract at E2 that does not alter WP603 authority, then test at E4 on matched sealed tasks whether R0/R1/R2 outcomes differ enough to justify adaptive selection after token/model-call/latency normalization.
